audit_feature: Bring the current audit screen into the conversation
codex_behavior: Appshots attach the frontmost window image and available accessibility text to a desktop chat. Text coverage depends on the source application; macOS/Windows permissions and client support govern availability.
trigger: The auditor chooses to share the current application window with a task.
audit_action: Examine the supplied screen in the context of the audit task, explain unfamiliar fields, identify apparent inconsistencies, and request underlying data when the capture cannot support a conclusion.
auditor_control: Choose the window and purpose; inspect what was captured before relying on it or sharing further.
example: While reviewing a loan-system rate configuration screen, ask which fields should be reconciled to the approved change request.
adaptation_boundary: A capture is a limited point-in-time input. It does not establish complete configuration history, actual application execution, or access to hidden records.

subfeatures.audit: Bring the current evidence or system screen into the task
Provide readable labels and values alongside the image

subfeatures.codex: Attach the capture to a chat
subfeatures.audit: Keep the supplied screen linked to the resulting analysis

audit_enhancements.change: Attach capture time, application/source identity and declared coverage to the shared screen.
audit_enhancements.why: A reviewer needs to distinguish what was actually supplied from unseen source-system data.

audit_feature: Review audit work and business changes for supported findings
codex_behavior: Codex analyses repository state and tool results; dedicated review examines selected changes and returns prioritised findings without modifying the working tree. GitHub review is a separate configured entry point.
trigger: An auditor requests review of a workpaper/change, or a configured review event starts it.
inputs: Selected workpaper or change and baseline
audit_action: Inspect audit scripts or authorised application code directly, and adapt the same review loop to changed workpapers or business-process evidence. Test supplied expectations and return located findings, impact and proposed corrections separately from applying them.
auditor_control: Select scope and criteria, challenge findings, and separately authorise corrections and professional sign-off.
example: Review a revised reconciliation workbook and flag an excluded account, a broken formula, and an unsupported conclusion with cell/source references.
adaptation_boundary: The review pattern transfers directly; audit-specific assertions and tests require explicit procedures and evidence. A clean review is not assurance beyond the work performed.

subfeatures.audit: Review changed cells, passages, rules, or records against their prior state
Rank evidenced exceptions under the chosen audit criteria
Return review notes before any corrective changes

audit_enhancements.change: Replace code-location review anchors with cell, document, record and evidence anchors.
audit_enhancements.why: Audit findings must be traceable to the affected work and its support.

audit_enhancements.change: Use the engagement's criteria and significance scheme for findings.
audit_enhancements.why: Developer severity labels do not determine audit significance or professional conclusions.

audit_feature: Control, application-security and findings workbench
codex_behavior: Codex Security provides specialised scans, change review, finding triage, remediation and verification through distinct local, cloud and programmatic surfaces. Cloud availability includes research-preview limits; it differs from Codex's own execution safeguards.
trigger: The auditor starts a targeted/bulk assessment or enables an authorised change-monitoring run.
inputs: Authorised application source and revision when performing actual software-security work
audit_action: Retain actual security scanning for authorised IT/IS audit of application code. Adapt the scan-and-review loop to supplied business-control procedures: consolidate exceptions, investigate evidence, propose improvements and retest while preserving coverage.
auditor_control: Set scope, validate findings, accept or dispute classifications, and decide whether remediation is sufficient.
example: Scan user-access extracts across several systems, investigate conflicting privileged roles, and retest an updated access population after remediation.
adaptation_boundary: Actual code-security capabilities remain useful for authorised IT/IS audit. General business-control tests require different tools and procedures; their proposed mirror preserves the work loop. Enterprise risk ownership needs separate domain design, with no delivery phase selected here.

subfeatures.audit: Focused control testing and bounded population-wide checks
Investigate and classify exceptions
Propose corrective action and test supplied remediation
Produce portable findings and follow-up evidence
Retain authorised application-security assessment for IT/IS audit
Reassess the affected scope after a relevant code or business change
Compare preventive control or process improvements grounded in findings

audit_enhancements.change: Supply audit-specific control tests and population reconciliation checks.
audit_enhancements.why: A vulnerability scanner's rules cannot test arbitrary business controls.

audit_enhancements.change: Separate suggested exceptions, validated findings and retest outcomes.
audit_enhancements.why: The auditor must know which conclusions have supporting investigation and review.

audit_feature: Contextual workpaper editing and review conversations
codex_behavior: Desktop editing and PR Chat place supported files or pull-request context beside conversation. Users can annotate content, request changes, inspect proposed patches, and accept or reject edits in supported flows.
trigger: The auditor opens an artifact or proposed change and selects content for discussion.
audit_action: Keep the discussion anchored to the selected work, explain its reasoning, prepare a targeted revision, and show the proposed result before incorporating it into the working artifact.
auditor_control: Edit directly or in the preferred external tool; decide which revisions to accept and separately perform any professional approval.
example: Select a finding's cause statement in a Word report, ask for stronger supporting reasoning, and review the proposed wording beside its evidence.
adaptation_boundary: Audit cell/document-aware review needs format-specific presentation. Accepting an edit does not sign off the workpaper, and a shared file does not require an editor API.

subfeatures.codex: Edit supported content in the desktop
subfeatures.audit: Inspect and edit supported audit artifacts in context
Anchor a review request to a specific passage or data area
Review and apply individual proposed artifact changes

audit_enhancements.change: Show format-aware changes in cells, formulas, report passages and evidence links.
audit_enhancements.why: Raw code-style patches can hide material workbook or document changes.

audit_enhancements.change: Keep edit acceptance distinct from any configured professional sign-off.
audit_enhancements.why: Accepting wording does not establish that the underlying evidence is sufficient.

audit_feature: Reviewable audit deliverables in familiar formats
codex_behavior: Codex produces text and file changes, with supported desktop previews and annotations for several document formats. Terminal and IDE surfaces present outputs differently and do not all offer the same visual review experience.
trigger: A task produces a workbook, report, slide deck, PDF, or other supported output.
audit_action: Create or revise the deliverable, present a suitable preview, support contextual feedback, and leave the saved artifact available for continued work in Excel, Word, PowerPoint, or another appropriate application.
auditor_control: Choose where to review/edit, request corrections, and decide when the output is ready for distribution.
example: Produce an exception workbook and committee presentation, inspect each in the workbench, then refine the presentation in PowerPoint.
adaptation_boundary: Format fidelity, formulas, comments, and save/reopen behavior must be verified. Previewing an artifact does not prove all its calculations or metadata are correct.

subfeatures.audit: Produce reusable workpapers, reports, and presentations
Inspect outputs beside the conversation
Request targeted revisions without re-describing the whole deliverable
Continue reviewing the same files in existing audit tools

audit_enhancements.change: Verify round-trip fidelity for supported workbook, document and slide features.
audit_enhancements.why: Continued work in external tools depends on preserving usable artifacts.

audit_enhancements.change: Detect intervening saved changes before revising an artifact.
audit_enhancements.why: Agent output must not silently overwrite the auditor's newer work.

audit_feature: Create and publish audit dashboards and lightweight tools
codex_behavior: Supported Sites flows create, refine, save, and deploy websites or applications. The documented public-beta managed publishing surface differs from CLI/IDE source editing; saved non-deployed versions can be reviewed before deployment.
trigger: The auditor asks for an interactive output or chooses to publish a reviewed version.
audit_action: Build an explorable exception dashboard or small audit utility, inspect its calculations and interactions, revise it through conversation, then publish only through an authorised hosting route.
auditor_control: Approve the data audience and release separately from creating the draft; inspect interactions and data handling.
example: Create a dashboard for exploring aged reconciliations with filters and drill-through references, then publish the reviewed version for the intended team.
adaptation_boundary: This mirrors a build-and-publish capability. A generated dashboard is not automatically a durable audit record system; hosting, access, and data storage remain distinct concerns.

subfeatures.codex: Create or refine an app from instructions
subfeatures.audit: Build a small audit analysis or reporting tool
Validate the interactive output before release
Publish the approved tool to its authorised audience

audit_enhancements.change: Carry source period, calculation definitions and evidence links into audit dashboards.
audit_enhancements.why: Interactive summaries need an inspectable basis for reliance.

audit_enhancements.change: Apply explicit audience and data-release choices to publishing.
audit_enhancements.why: A useful working dashboard may contain information that cannot be shared with its default audience.

audit_feature: Core audit work tools available to the agent
codex_behavior: Codex surfaces expose tools for files, execution, images, search and agent operations according to the environment. Tool availability, permission to use a tool, and a completed invocation are separate states.
trigger: An audit task requires a supported file, calculation, search, or agent operation.
audit_action: Select and call the relevant tool, inspect its result, and use the result in the next step. Keep concrete operations visible so the auditor can connect claims to actual file reads, calculations, or changes.
auditor_control: Set operating scope, review consequential actions, and interrupt or redirect the task.
example: Read an expenses CSV, run a duplicate-payment query, inspect candidate matches, and create a workbook for review.
adaptation_boundary: An audit-facing label does not itself supply a new execution engine or permission. Domain-specific tools extend the same mechanism; their correctness needs separate validation.

subfeatures.audit: Inspect evidence and prepare working outputs
Execute reproducible analysis
Distinguish performed tests from intended work

audit_enhancements.change: Provide format-aware extraction and calculation tools with inspectable results.
audit_enhancements.why: Office artifacts and audit populations need more than plain-text editing.

audit_feature: Discover and manage available audit data connections
codex_behavior: Codex app integrations have catalog, installation and effective callable states. Enabled configuration, identity and policy affect access; connector traffic follows a distinct control path from sandboxed shell networking.
trigger: The auditor selects a connected service or asks what sources/actions are available.
audit_action: Show which integration can actually supply the requested material, use its permitted operations, and identify the acting account and destination before a side effect.
outputs: Retrieved material or confirmed action result
auditor_control: Connect the intended account, limit scope, and authorise consequential writes.
example: Retrieve an approved policy from a connected repository while leaving an unrelated client connection unavailable to the engagement.
adaptation_boundary: Shared local files remain usable without an app connector. A catalog listing does not prove support for a particular audit object or operation.

subfeatures.audit: Discover permitted audit information sources
Explain whether a connection can perform the requested operation now
Make the acting account and record destination explicit

audit_enhancements.change: Display the client/entity scope and effective read/write actions of each connection.
audit_enhancements.why: The same app may contain data from unrelated engagements or clients.

audit_feature: Connect reusable audit tools through a standard tool interface
codex_behavior: Codex connects to local or remote MCP servers supplying tools, resources and prompts. Connections and authentication are explicit; tools may read or mutate systems. App-server uses a different protocol from MCP.
trigger: The task needs a capability supplied by a configured MCP server.
audit_action: Discover the supported operation, supply bounded inputs, execute it through the connection, and inspect the result before incorporating evidence or recording a claimed update.
auditor_control: Choose trusted connections and permitted operations; review writes separately from reads.
example: Use a read-only database tool to obtain a loan-rate change population, then use a separate analysis tool to test effective dates.
adaptation_boundary: MCP supplies an interface, not audit semantics or a universal connector. A remote tool's authority and data path need individual assessment.

subfeatures.audit: Attach local analytics or approved remote audit services
Retrieve task references and reusable tool-specific guidance
Confirm identity and available read/write actions

audit_enhancements.change: Require source identity, extraction scope and observation time in evidence-returning tools.
audit_enhancements.why: Structured tool output needs enough context to assess relevance and freshness.

audit_feature: Installable audit capability packages
codex_behavior: Plugins bundle skills and other capabilities such as MCP tools, hooks or UI. Curated and team/project distribution paths exist; installing a package and authorising its capabilities are distinct, with client-specific support.
trigger: The auditor or administrator adds or updates an approved capability package.
inputs: Tool credentials and policy where needed
audit_action: Make packaged procedures, references and tools available to the workbench while exposing their ownership and effective permissions. Allow the team to reuse a consistent capability set across relevant workspaces.
auditor_control: Choose package scope, inspect included behavior, and enable only permitted connections or actions.
example: Install a team package containing access-review procedures, an approved export parser, and reporting templates.
adaptation_boundary: Installation does not approve an audit methodology or grant source access. Preserve separate owners and update paths for workspace, personal and plugin-provided skills.

subfeatures.audit: Package reusable audit procedures with the tools they use
Share approved practice or team capability packages
Inspect versions, updates, disablement and removal

audit_enhancements.change: Declare supported practices, input formats, dependencies and procedure versions in an audit package.
audit_enhancements.why: A team needs to understand where a reusable package applies and what an update changes.

audit_feature: Reusable audit procedures invoked through conversation
codex_behavior: Skills package instructions with optional references, scripts and resources. Codex can select a relevant skill or run one explicitly requested by the user; skill ownership and distribution differ by source.
trigger: The auditor invokes a procedure, or the agent recognises a matching task.
audit_action: Follow the reusable procedure with the current inputs, execute permitted supporting tools, and return the procedure's expected work product and verification evidence.
auditor_control: Choose or adjust the procedure and inspect its assumptions, inputs and resulting work.
example: Invoke a bank-reconciliation skill with this month's statements and ledger export, then review the reconciling items in the generated workbook.
adaptation_boundary: A skill guides execution and does not grant data access. Procedure criteria, version references and required task-level checks belong to the direct audit counterpart. Formal methodology governance requires separate domain design; no delivery phase is selected here.

subfeatures.audit: Run a named audit procedure
Suggest an applicable working method
Keep instructions, calculations and templates together

audit_enhancements.change: Include criteria references, required inputs, expected outputs and verification steps in audit procedure skills.
audit_enhancements.why: A reusable routine must explain what was tested and how its result should be checked.

audit_feature: Teach the assistant a demonstrated audit routine
codex_behavior: On supported macOS setups, Record & Replay observes a permitted demonstration and drafts a reusable skill. Later runs use current task tools and variable inputs; Computer Use availability is required.
trigger: The auditor chooses to record a familiar repeatable procedure, then later invokes the resulting skill.
audit_action: Capture the demonstrated steps, draft an inspectable procedure with inputs and verification guidance, let the auditor refine it, and repeat it with new values under the current task's permissions.
auditor_control: Start/stop recording, inspect the generated procedure, provide new inputs, and review replay outcomes.
example: Demonstrate downloading a monthly control report, filtering the period, and saving it under the engagement's naming convention.
adaptation_boundary: Recording is not proof that the demonstrated method is appropriate or that replay succeeded. The reference is macOS-specific; matching it elsewhere requires investigation.

subfeatures.audit: Demonstrate an existing audit routine
Turn the demonstration into an inspectable reusable procedure
Repeat for another period, entity, or population

audit_enhancements.change: Add review of captured assumptions and validation on a second representative case before routine reuse.
audit_enhancements.why: A demonstrated path may omit exceptions or depend on unnoticed application state.

audit_feature: Workspace guidance and operating preferences
codex_behavior: Codex discovers applicable AGENTS.md guidance and combines configuration with managed requirements under defined precedence. Settings control models, tools, permissions and other behavior, and some configuration can live outside the project.
trigger: An audit workspace or scoped task starts, resumes, or changes its applicable configuration.
audit_action: Apply the relevant vocabulary, file conventions, preferred procedures and operating limits to work in that scope. Make inherited guidance inspectable when it affects an outcome.
auditor_control: Maintain workspace instructions and inspect which higher-level requirements apply.
example: A client workspace specifies financial year, entity naming, working-paper conventions, approved criteria references and read-only access to source extracts.
adaptation_boundary: Instructions shape agent behavior; they are not by themselves enforced access controls or proof of methodology compliance. Engagement facts still need identified sources.

subfeatures.audit: Apply the relevant client, engagement and folder guidance
Combine practitioner preferences with organisational limits
Tailor operating behavior without changing the underlying workspace experience

audit_enhancements.change: Expose the effective client/engagement guidance and its provenance.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditors must identify which conventions and criteria shaped the task.

audit_feature: Checks at agent workflow events
codex_behavior: Hooks react to supported agent lifecycle events using configured handlers. MCP hooks use existing connections; an explicit blocking result can stop an operation, while missing tools or errors do not inherently block it.
trigger: A configured agent event occurs, such as a tool call, compaction, task start or completion.
audit_action: Run an appropriate contextual or output check at that lifecycle point and report its result. For example, validate a generated workpaper's required references after an edit and surface any gap before the auditor relies on it.
auditor_control: Approve trusted handlers, inspect their scope, and decide how an unmet or failed check affects the workflow.
example: After the agent writes an exception workbook, check that its population source and test parameters are recorded.
adaptation_boundary: Lifecycle hooks do not themselves detect business events such as rate changes. Their reference failure behavior is not a fail-closed compliance guarantee or immutable audit trail.

subfeatures.audit: Check intended actions and generated work
Restore essential task guidance on continuation
Surface required completion checks and handoff information

audit_enhancements.change: Define the consequence of a failed or unavailable mandatory audit check separately from the reference hook default.
audit_enhancements.why: The current hook failure behavior does not establish that required checks ran or blocked subsequent reliance.

audit_feature: A workbench client that can drive and observe the agent runtime
codex_behavior: App-server exposes thread operations, streamed activity, tools, configuration and approval exchanges to a rich client over JSON-RPC. Its command and WebSocket transport are experimental; individual execution methods have different authority.
trigger: The workbench starts a task, resumes work, displays activity, or answers an agent request.
audit_action: Present the familiar conversational workspace while the runtime performs permitted work. Translate runtime events into understandable audit-task progress, artifact changes, input requests, errors and completion states.
outputs: Human response events and resumable work
auditor_control: Steer, inspect, interrupt and approve applicable actions through the workspace.
example: While testing expenses, show the active data extraction, completed calculation, missing evidence request and resulting workbook in one task.
adaptation_boundary: This maps the runtime/client contract, not a selected architecture. Experimental status, service eligibility and each method's effective authority require verification; a single protocol does not imply one sandbox boundary.

subfeatures.audit: Start, continue and stop audit work
Explain actual progress and generated outputs
Let the auditor resolve a specific permission or clarification request

audit_enhancements.change: Translate runtime events into audit-task, evidence and artifact status without overstating completion.
audit_enhancements.why: Tool completion, successful analysis and accepted audit work are different states.

audit_feature: Task-specific tools supplied by the audit workspace
codex_behavior: The experimental dynamic-tools API lets a client describe tools and fulfil runtime tool requests through item/tool/call. It requires opt-in and is distinct from configuring an external MCP server.
trigger: An agent requests a tool that the current workspace has exposed.
audit_action: Expose bounded operations appropriate to the current audit context, fulfil a requested operation through the host, and return a structured result that the agent can inspect.
outputs: Tool result linked to its invocation
auditor_control: Operate within the workspace's authorised scope and review consequential changes; an agent-proposed call does not determine its own authority.
example: A workpaper view exposes a tool to fetch a selected sample's evidence references without giving the agent access to unrelated engagements.
adaptation_boundary: The tool mechanism is a direct counterpart; specific native record operations depend on the later record-mode design. Experimental API and host-side enforcement remain unresolved implementation questions.

subfeatures.codex: Supply tool definitions at thread start
subfeatures.audit: Offer context-relevant audit operations
Perform a bounded operation under host authority
Make the result and any failed action explicit

audit_enhancements.change: Bind each audit-specific host tool to the current artifact/entity and validate returned identifiers.
audit_enhancements.why: Task-specific operations must not act on unrelated or stale audit material.

feature: Codex SDK, non-interactive execution, and GitHub Action
audit_feature: Run audit procedures from scripts and event-driven jobs
codex_behavior: Codex offers SDKs, non-interactive exec and a GitHub Action for programmatic tasks. They provide distinct runtime interfaces and maturity levels, with structured events available for supported batch or CI workflows.
trigger: A script, scheduler or configured external event starts a bounded job.
audit_action: Run the declared analysis without an interactive foreground session, retain its structured outcome and artifacts, and route a completed, failed or needs-attention result to the auditor.
auditor_control: Configure the mandate and limits beforehand; review exceptions and authorise any consequential follow-up.
example: A detected approved interest-rate change starts a job that tests specified approval and effective-date controls against the relevant evidence.
adaptation_boundary: The automation runner does not create an event feed or prove control compliance. Source access, duplicate-event handling and missed/failed runs require explicit design and validation. Ephemeral rollout behavior does not delete generated files, external records or other copies; retain relied-on work according to the chosen policy.

subfeatures.audit: Call a reusable audit task from another authorised tool
Run a bounded assurance job without a foreground conversation
Start a configured test when a relevant business change is detected
Track completion, errors and generated results
Start, observe and continue a programmatic audit investigation
Run an eligible transient task without retaining its runtime rollout

audit_enhancements.change: Bind automated runs to an event/source version, procedure version and bounded population.
audit_enhancements.why: Results must identify exactly which change and evidence were tested.

audit_enhancements.change: Surface missed, duplicate, failed and inconclusive runs distinctly from passed checks.
audit_enhancements.why: Continuous assurance requires visibility into coverage and execution gaps.

feature: Task entry points from connected services
audit_feature: Receive audit requests and change-triggered reviews where work already happens
codex_behavior: Configured integrations can create or route Codex tasks from services such as GitHub, GitLab, Slack or Linear; selected enterprise flows use Teams. Hosted execution, availability and maturity depend on the integration.
trigger: A permitted mention, request, ticket transition or configured service event arrives.
audit_action: Create or continue a scoped task from that source, obtain the permitted supporting material, perform the requested review, and return findings or a task link to the appropriate destination.
outputs: Task linked to its source item
Review findings or requested work product
auditor_control: Define eligible events, accounts and destinations; distinguish a request to test from authority to approve or change records.
example: A change ticket moves to ready-for-review and invokes the assurance agent to inspect approval, segregation and implementation evidence.
adaptation_boundary: A business event adapter is an audit-specific counterpart to the service integration. Its availability is not established by Codex's GitHub integration; ordinary saved-file work remains independent.

subfeatures.codex: Mention the agent in a service
subfeatures.audit: Request assistance from the existing work conversation

subfeatures.codex: Route service context into a task
subfeatures.audit: Carry the originating change/request into audit analysis

subfeatures.codex: Return results to the originating work
subfeatures.audit: Make review findings actionable beside the relevant item

audit_enhancements.change: Define business-event adapters, qualifying events and audit context requirements.
audit_enhancements.why: A PR event integration does not automatically observe loan-rate or other business-process changes.

audit_enhancements.change: Bind returned findings to the originating change and intended reviewer.
audit_enhancements.why: The person receiving a result needs to know which event it addresses.

audit_feature: Delegate parallel audit work to specialised assistants
codex_behavior: Codex delegates tasks to separate agent threads and combines results. Custom agents can specialise instructions and supported model settings; they inherit parent permissions, provider and MCP connections rather than independently expanding access.
trigger: The auditor or coordinating agent divides suitable work into independent tasks.
audit_action: Assign separate agents to population analysis, criteria research, evidence inspection or workpaper review, track their work, and reconcile their findings into a coherent result with visible disagreements.
auditor_control: Inspect delegated scope and progress, redirect tasks, and verify the synthesis before relying on it.
example: One agent checks rate-change approvals, another recalculates affected interest, and a third reviews customer-notification evidence.
adaptation_boundary: Parallel agents are not automatically independent assurance providers. Shared assumptions can produce correlated mistakes; formal human review remains a separate decision.

subfeatures.audit: Split evidence and testing work by question
Reuse distinct analysis or review roles
Trace a result back to the delegated work
Reconcile findings and surface disagreement

audit_enhancements.change: Require delegated results to identify evidence, method and unresolved disagreements.
audit_enhancements.why: The coordinating agent must reconcile substantive support rather than count agreeing agents.

feature: Side chats, fork, and task references
audit_feature: Explore audit questions without losing the main work
codex_behavior: Side chats and forks create separate conversational paths for focused questions or alternative approaches. Supported clients can reference other tasks and navigate between related work without rewriting the original transcript.
trigger: The auditor opens a side investigation or tries a different approach from existing context.
audit_action: Investigate a specific issue separately, preserve the main engagement conversation, and bring relevant conclusions back with a clear reference to the supporting branch.
outputs: Referenced conclusion for the main task
auditor_control: Choose what context is carried, compare paths, and identify which conclusion is adopted or superseded.
example: Fork a sampling discussion to explore a different stratification while keeping the original test approach available for comparison.
adaptation_boundary: Forking a conversation does not itself isolate working files, change permissions, or create an approved alternative procedure. Avoid treating an abandoned branch as the current conclusion.

subfeatures.audit: Investigate a narrow evidence or methodology question
Explore an alternative interpretation from the same starting context
Link the supporting investigation into the main work

audit_enhancements.change: Show which exploratory conclusion was adopted or superseded.
audit_enhancements.why: Alternative analyses must not be mistaken for the current relied-on conclusion.

audit_feature: Separate working copies for parallel audit analysis
codex_behavior: Git worktrees give independent tasks separate working directories in the same repository. App-managed copies can have different lifecycles; isolation and handoff behavior vary across local, remote and scheduled workflows.
trigger: The auditor or agent starts parallel work that could modify overlapping artifacts.
audit_action: Give each analysis a separate working copy, preserve the starting version, and compare completed outputs before integrating selected changes into the main body of work.
auditor_control: Choose which changes to retain and resolve conflicting edits before replacing the shared artifact.
example: Analyse alternate loan populations in separate copies of a workbook, then incorporate the selected result without overwriting the other analyst's work.
adaptation_boundary: This is the isolation pattern, not a requirement to use Git for every Office artifact. Binary document merging needs format-aware handling; filesystem separation does not establish engagement confidentiality.

subfeatures.audit: Protect concurrent analysis from accidental file overwrites
Know which source version each analysis used
Reconcile completed work into the main artifact

audit_enhancements.change: Provide format-aware comparison and explicit reconciliation of Office artifact changes.
audit_enhancements.why: Separate working copies alone do not safely merge binary or structured document edits.

audit_feature: Maintain task focus through long audit work
codex_behavior: Codex carries instructions, conversation and tool results in active context. Automatic or requested compaction condenses earlier material for continuation; it reduces context pressure without guaranteeing that every prior detail survives.
trigger: A long-running audit conversation approaches its context limit or requests compaction.
inputs: References to durable files and decisions
audit_action: Continue the task from a concise state of its objective, completed work and next steps, reopening identified artifacts whenever exact evidence, calculations or wording are required.
outputs: Resumed work linked to durable artifacts
Questions where needed context is missing
auditor_control: Inspect the current scope, restate a correction, and require source verification for material conclusions.
example: Resume a multi-day payroll analysis with the population file, completed tests and unresolved exceptions still identified.
adaptation_boundary: A condensed conversation is working context, not the evidence archive. Exact facts, approved criteria and relied-on outputs should remain in accessible artifacts or records.

subfeatures.audit: Keep the current objective and relevant work available
Continue lengthy investigations within context limits
Verify exact evidence instead of relying on a summary

audit_enhancements.change: Keep evidence identifiers, criteria references and material decisions in durable task artifacts.
audit_enhancements.why: Compaction can omit details that should remain recoverable for audit work.

audit_feature: Return to prior audit work and its reasoning
codex_behavior: Supported Codex clients provide thread listing, resumption, search, branching, archiving and deletion. Available operations and storage differ between local, cloud and remote environments; structured runtime history supports continuation.
trigger: The auditor returns to earlier work, locates a prior discussion, or manages its lifecycle.
audit_action: Find the relevant task, recover its previous instructions and results, check current source versions, and continue with a new question or action without pretending the old context is current evidence.
outputs: Updated task status or archive state
auditor_control: Choose what to resume, retain, archive or delete within applicable policy.
example: Find the prior discussion explaining an exception rule, reopen the supporting workbook, and revise the analysis for a new period.
adaptation_boundary: Conversation persistence is distinct from formal audit-record retention. Deleting a chat does not necessarily remove exported files, and a past accessible source may no longer be authorised.

subfeatures.audit: Find earlier analysis and its working context
Continue unfinished audit work
Manage task history under the applicable policy

audit_enhancements.change: Link history to artifact versions and distinguish task-history retention from retained audit records.
audit_enhancements.why: Resuming a discussion should not silently reuse superseded evidence or imply formal record preservation.

audit_feature: Controlled recall of useful audit working preferences
codex_behavior: Local Codex memory is a separate store, off by default. Eligible prior chats can contribute useful context; machine and chat controls govern use and contribution, with background generation and deletion controls.
trigger: Memory is enabled and a new task can benefit from eligible prior context.
audit_action: Recall useful conventions or previously learned tool details, identify them as recalled context, and check current authoritative sources before using them as audit facts or criteria.
auditor_control: Enable or disable memory use/contribution for the task and remove unwanted memory through supported controls.
example: Recall the team's preferred exception workbook layout while reading current-period facts directly from the supplied data.
adaptation_boundary: Reuse must respect engagement/client scope and current access. Memory is not a substitute for a current policy, transaction record or approval; cross-engagement controls still need explicit adaptation.

subfeatures.audit: Remember permitted working conventions
Keep a sensitive assignment from informing future tasks
Correct or remove unwanted retained working context

audit_enhancements.change: Apply client/engagement scope and current-access checks to reusable recall.
audit_enhancements.why: Useful preferences must not carry confidential evidence or stale conclusions into an unrelated assignment.

audit_feature: Optional recall of the auditor's recent application work
codex_behavior: Computer History is an optional macOS feature using allowed-app interaction/accessibility events to create a searchable timeline and local memories. It has distinct opt-in, processing and retention behavior and excludes screenshots and private browsing.
trigger: The auditor enables permitted app/site capture and later asks about recent work.
audit_action: Help locate a recently used file, reconstruct a working sequence or recover the context of a prior activity, then open original materials for any substantive audit analysis.
auditor_control: Choose permitted apps/sites, pause collection, and manage deletion and memory settings.
example: Locate the report the auditor examined before revising an exception workpaper and return to the original saved file.
adaptation_boundary: Ambient recall is optional assistance, not employee surveillance or a complete audit trail. The reference has local storage plus server processing; local memory files alone do not establish local-only processing.

subfeatures.audit: Scope optional recent-work context
Locate previously inspected work
Recover useful context while verifying against original materials

audit_enhancements.change: Label ambient summaries as activity-derived context and maintain explicit app/client boundaries.
audit_enhancements.why: Recent activity can aid navigation but cannot stand in for verified audit evidence.

feature: Durable instructions vs memory vs skills
audit_feature: Keep audit rules, procedures, recall and task history distinct
codex_behavior: Codex separates durable project instructions, reusable skills, recalled memory and conversation history. These context sources have different ownership, lifecycle and authority; their roles should not be conflated.
trigger: A task gathers context or encounters conflicting guidance.
inputs: Recalled context and current task history
audit_action: Use instructions for enduring workspace rules, skills for repeatable methods, memory for helpful recall, and the conversation for current direction. Verify material facts in identified evidence and make conflicts visible.
auditor_control: Choose the intended procedure, update durable guidance deliberately, and correct recalled preferences without silently changing policy.
example: Apply the engagement's approved criteria, use a sampling procedure, recall a formatting preference, and keep this period's exceptions in its own task files.
adaptation_boundary: The separation transfers directly. Formal methodology versioning, professional approval and cross-client knowledge rules require domain design; memory must not silently replace them.

subfeatures.audit: Workspace rules and lasting engagement guidance
Reusable working procedures
Helpful permitted recall
Current task directions and working discussion

audit_enhancements.change: Display whether a material instruction came from policy, a procedure, memory or the current request.
audit_enhancements.why: Different context sources have different authority and should not silently override one another.
